intro: You are in Kars Museum, a museum in Kars province founded in 1959. It holds the finds from the Ani excavations, and in its garden, Russian-era steam engines and church bells tell the story of the city's last two centuries.
history: Founded in 1959, the museum became the central collection for the excavations at Ani. But the city itself is also its subject. Kars was under Russian rule between 1878 and 1918, so its last two centuries are part of the story here, and railway engines and machinery from those years stand in the garden.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the finds from Ani, the Urartian works, the Russian-period collection and the Ethnography hall.
facts: Did you know? The church bells in the garden were gathered from abandoned churches in the region, each one the last remaining trace of a different congregation. Together with the steam engines, they belong to the Russian period at Kars, between 1878 and 1918. And the museum is the central collection for the excavations at Ani.
outro: This brings our tour of Kars Museum to an end. Before you go, please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
